operations.evidence: The accredited publication covers offender management statistics for October to December 2025, annual 2025 figures, and the prison population at 31 March 2026.
The publication is for England and Wales and does not provide parcel-level or exact-address evidence.
The prison population was 87,342 on 31 March 2026, around 1% lower than at the same point in 2025.
A national custody total cannot identify local public-safety conditions at a parcel.
The sentenced prison population was 70,829, representing 81% of the total on 31 March 2026.
Custody composition is not a geographic risk score.
The remand prison population was 16,025, representing 18% of the total on 31 March 2026.
The remand population cannot be attributed to any neighbourhood or property.
The non-criminal prison population was 488, representing 1% of the total on 31 March 2026.
This aggregate category does not support parcel inference.
The month-end prison population reached 88,423 at the end of August 2025.
A national month-end peak is not evidence of local incident exposure.
The prison population was 87,465 at the end of September 2025 after falling by around 1,000 from August.
The month-to-month national movement does not identify local causation.
The remand population decreased by 9% between 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2026.
The annual change is system-level and not suitable for parcel scoring.
The untried remand population was 10,585 on 31 March 2026, down 7% from March 2025.
Pre-conviction custody statistics must not be interpreted as neighbourhood crime prevalence.
The convicted unsentenced remand population was 5,440 on 31 March 2026, down 13% from March 2025.
The figure is an institutional caseload measure, not an address-level measure.
Violence against the person and drug offences were the two largest offence groups among people held on remand.
Offence-group composition in custody cannot establish risk around a particular parcel.
White prisoners comprised 73% of the sentenced population and 64% of the remand population.
Demographic proportions must not be used to infer risk about individuals, groups, or locations.
The sentenced population increased by 1% compared with March 2025.
The change is national and cannot be mapped to a property.
Populations serving 12 months to less than 2 years and 2 years to less than 4 years each increased by 11% from the previous year.
Sentence-length changes do not indicate local safety conditions.
